subject: general
question: P and Q together can complete a piece of work in 20 days. Q and R together can complete it in 30 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days can Q alone complete it?
solution:
**Given**

P and Q together can complete the work in 20 days.

Q and R together can complete it in 30 days.

P is twice as good a workman as R.

**Concept used:**

Work done = Efficiency × Time, where Efficiency is the ability to do work.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units

Efficiency of P and Q = 60/20 = 3 ...........(i)

Efficiency of Q and R = 60/30 = 2 ...........(ii)

Acc to given condition

Efficiency of P : Efficiency of R = 2 : 1

Adding equation (i) and (ii), we get

Efficiency of (P + 2Q + R) = 5

⇒ 2 + 2Q + 1 = 

⇒ 2Q = 2

 

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 1

 

Days taken by Q to complete the work alone = 60/1 = 60 days

 

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**
